summary: Buzz Products is a Melbourne-based designer of travel amenities, founded in 1999 by Barry Gold, that made two acquisitions in 2023 and launched several airline products at AIX 2026. Revenue is known only from third-party estimates that range from $24.6 million to $92.9 million, and headcount reportedly fell 4% in a slow-growing market with established rivals Formia and WESSCO International. No high-severity risk appears, but traction is not independently verified, so more diligence is needed before committing.

facts.text: Buzz Products designs and makes passenger amenities, skincare, serviceware, children's items, sleepwear and textiles for airlines, hotels, cruise lines and rail operators.

evidence.quote: Buzz Products is an Abbotsford, Victoria-based company that designs and manufactures passenger amenities, skincare, serviceware, children's items, sleepwear, and textiles for the global travel and leisure industry
We partner with luxury brands to create iconic product collaborations across the travel industry – from luxury amenities and skincare to serviceware, textiles, and children’s products
For more than 25 years, Buzz has designed and created luxury products for travellers including airline amenity kits, hotel bathroom amenities, sleepwear, and children’s products

facts.text: The company was founded in 1999, is privately held and is headquartered in Abbotsford, Melbourne, Australia.

evidence.quote: Buzz Products was originally founded in 1999 by Managing Director Barry Gold

facts.text: Third-party data providers estimate annual revenue at $24.6 million for 2026 at one source and $92.9 million with 306 employees at another.

evidence.quote: The Buzz Products annual revenue was $24.6 million in 2026
Buzz Products's estimated annual revenue is currently $92.9Mper year.(i)

facts.text: Buzz Products bought sustainability brand Single Use Ain't Sexy in July 2023 for an undisclosed sum, with plans to put its products in more than 50,000 hotel rooms worldwide.

evidence.quote: Buzz Products has purchased Single Use Ain’t Sexy for an undisclosed sum

facts.text: Buzz Products acquired pyjama start-up Recliner in October 2023, after the two had collaborated since 2019.

evidence.quote: The pyjama brand has been collaborating with Buzz since 2019, creating exclusive sleep products for its travel partner American Airlines in 2022

facts.text: Trade outlet APEX reported that Buzz unveiled multiple airline product launches at AIX 2026, including Business Class and Premium Economy amenity kits.

evidence.quote: Developed with Buzz, the collection introduces amenity kits for both Business Class and Premium Economy passengers

facts.text: Buzz Products is a participant in the UN Global Compact Network Australia, having joined in December 2024.

evidence.quote: the organization officially became a participant in the United Nations Global Compact in December 2024

facts.text: The company says it has collaborations such as Giorgio Armani for Etihad Airways, Emirates First Class loungewear and Lanvin Parfums for Turkish Airlines; this client list is self-reported.

evidence.quote: Giorgio Armani for Etihad Airways

facts.text: Direct competitors include Formia, which calls itself the market leader in travel amenities, and WESSCO International of Los Angeles.
